Play videos, music and photos from your PC, Mac or phone on your smart TV, or show it your screen. No app on the TV, no server to set up: OpusCast hands everything to the TV over your home network (DLNA / UPnP), so the TV remote keeps working.

For **Windows 10/11**, **macOS 12 Monterey or newer** (Intel and Apple silicon), **Linux** and **Android 8+**.

## Windows

Download **OpusCast-v1.0-Windows-Setup.exe** below (or the .zip to run it without installing).

- Windows SmartScreen will say it protected your PC: choose *More info* → *Run anyway* (the app isn't signed with a paid certificate).
- When Windows asks whether OpusCast may use the network, allow it on *Private networks*, so the TV can fetch your videos.
- Right-click a video, song or photo → *Open with* → *OpusCast*.

## macOS

Download **OpusCast-v1.0-macOS.dmg** below and drag OpusCast to Applications. One app for Intel and Apple silicon Macs, macOS 12 Monterey or newer.

- The app isn't signed by Apple, so the first time: right-click it → *Open* → *Open* (macOS 12–14), or on macOS 15 open it once, then System Settings → Privacy & Security → *Open Anyway*.
- To cast the desktop, allow OpusCast under *Screen Recording* when macOS asks, then start it again.
- macOS doesn't hand the Mac's sound to apps. To send it to the TV too, install [BlackHole](https://existential.audio/blackhole/) (free) and choose it as the output.

The Windows and macOS apps do everything the Linux app below does, with ffmpeg built in.

## Android

Download **OpusCast-v1.0.apk** below and open it on the phone (Android 8.0 or newer). Android asks you to allow installing apps from your browser or file manager.

- **Videos:** choose one, or use *Share → OpusCast* / *Open with → OpusCast*. Picks up where you left off, with the same subtitles. Subtitles inside MKV, WebM and MP4 videos, subtitle files next to the video (after you allow its folder), or any file you pick. SRT, ASS/SSA, WebVTT, SAMI and MicroDVD/SubViewer are converted for the TV; on Samsung TVs subtitles switch while the video plays.
- **Music:** pick several songs and they play one after another, with title, artist, album and cover on the TV and on the lock screen.
- **Photos:** a slideshow on the TV with swipe, Next / Previous and 3–30 s per photo. HEIC, WebP, rotated and very large photos are converted so the TV can show them.
- **Cast phone screen:** the phone's screen, and the sound apps play (Android 10+), live on the TV in 1080p or 720p, a second or two behind.
- **Left the phone's screen on the TV by mistake?** It stays shared: choose “OpusCast on *your phone*” in the TV's sources (Samsung: *Source*) and you're back, or tap *Show on the TV again* in the app or the notification. It can also come back by itself (*Bring it back if the TV leaves*). Only the TV you share to sees your screen there.
- *Show on phone*: a muted copy of the video on the phone, in step with the TV.
- The phone's volume buttons set the TV's volume. Lock-screen and Bluetooth media controls work too.
- Keeps serving with the screen off.

This is the first Android build, and it hasn't been tried on many phones and TVs yet. Please report what doesn't work. The APK is signed with a temporary key, so a later version won't install over this one: uninstall it first.

## Linux

```sh
git clone https://github.com/m1omg/OpusCast.git
cd OpusCast
./install.sh
```

- **Videos** with subtitles (files next to the video and tracks inside it), resume, and *Show on PC* (a muted copy in the window, in step with the TV).
- **Music:** songs or whole folders, one after another, with cover and tags on the TV. Formats the TV doesn't list (often Opus or Ogg) are converted to MP3 first.
- **Photos:** a slideshow; pick one photo to flip through its folder. HEIC, WebP, rotated and huge photos are converted on the way.
- **Cast the desktop:** the screen and the PC's sound live on the TV. Works on X11 (Cinnamon, MATE, Xfce, …), which other casting apps that rely on the screen-sharing portal can't do, and on Wayland (GNOME, KDE Plasma, …) through the desktop's own screen-sharing dialog.
- **Left the desktop on the TV by mistake?** It stays shared: choose “OpusCast on *your PC*” in the TV's sources (Samsung: *Source*) and you're back, or click *Show on the TV again* on the computer. It can also come back by itself (*Bring it back if the TV leaves* in the desktop options). Only the TV you share to sees your desktop there.
- Command line too: `opuscast VIDEO`, `opuscast SONGS…`, `opuscast PHOTOS… --every 8`, `opuscast --desktop`.

See the README for what to install on your distro.

## Both

- **Works with more TVs than Samsung:** OpusCast reads which formats each TV lists and uses that TV's own names for them, retries while a TV is still busy, and seeks the way the TV accepts. Tested with a Samsung; LG, Sony, Philips, Hisense, Panasonic and Android TV sets should work too.
- **Philips TVs:** if yours isn't found, turn on *Digital Media Renderer – DMR* (All Settings → Wireless and Networks → Wired or Wi-Fi).
- **Chromecast, Google TV streamers and the Nvidia Shield** only speak Google Cast, so OpusCast can't use them.
- **DLNA speakers** (Sonos and others) can be picked for music.
- A device list that shows what on your network can play video or music.
- The Skynet intro, off by default.
- English and Slovak.
